protocol.role: Supplementary analysis prespecified before held-out inference; primary protocol and all seven primary model results remain unchanged
protocol.weight_rule: uniform arithmetic mean of exported probability vectors; each member has weight 1/3
protocol.probability_processing: No fitting, recalibration, clipping, renormalization, threshold tuning or member selection
protocol.tie_rule: argmax takes the first class in the published class order
protocol.clinical_rule: Only the three multitask AD/CN heads; average already slice-aggregated subject probabilities within each source/split; MCI remains prediction-only
protocol.stage_uncertainty: Reuse primary paired bootstrap helper: 2000 context-seeded replicates, base seed 1729, two-sided 95% percentile intervals; prepared hash-group units for primary/sensitivity and image units for reused original100
protocol.clinical_uncertainty: Reuse exact Clopper-Pearson intervals for subject accuracy, AD sensitivity and CN specificity; no old-baseline AD/CN comparison
protocol.member_spread: Report every member's accuracy, balanced accuracy and macro F1; arithmetic mean, sample SD, minimum and maximum across the three prespecified seeds
protocol.disagreement: Any-member hard-prediction disagreement and each of the three pairwise disagreement rates on the same aligned cases; descriptive only
protocol.brier: Mean over cases of the SUM over classes of (probability minus one-hot reference)^2; range 0 to 2, not divided by class count
protocol.ece: Top-label ECE with ten fixed equal-width bins [0,.1),...,[.9,1]; sum of bin fraction times absolute bin accuracy minus mean maximum probability; empty bins contribute zero
protocol.calibration_interpretation: Brier and ECE are descriptive, uncalibrated probability summaries with no added confidence intervals; not clinical calibration evidence or selection criteria
protocol.decision_rule: Report both condition ensembles and all applicable cohorts regardless of results; no winner, promotion, deployment or additional training is selected from held-out outcomes
protocol.compute: CPU analysis of existing evaluator CSVs only; zero new GPU inference or training
limitations: Ensembling can retain correlated errors and does not fix missing patient provenance, source confounding or inadequate clinical data.
Original100 remains historically reused, and the primary exact-row comparison has known old development hash-group exposure; the secondary subset is not patient-independent.
Conditional bootstrap intervals do not account for training randomness or multiple comparisons; three-seed spread is not a confidence interval.
The clinical external pilot contains only one AD subject. Ensemble averaging does not increase the independent sample size.
Research inference with an ensemble requires three member forwards; no production inference wrapper is built or deployed by this analysis.

limitations: Ensembling can retain correlated errors and does not fix missing patient provenance, source confounding or inadequate clinical data.
Original100 remains historically reused, and the primary exact-row comparison has known old development hash-group exposure; the secondary subset is not patient-independent.
Conditional bootstrap intervals do not account for training randomness or multiple comparisons; three-seed spread is not a confidence interval.

Original100 is a historically reused image-level descriptive benchmark. The old checkpoint had 66 train, 9 validation and 25 test image matches; it is not independent clinical validation.
Legacy patient IDs and original augmentation families are unknown. Hash grouping is image similarity, not patient identity; cluster intervals do not establish clinical independence.

The full primary intersection holds out exact rows for both models, but includes hash groups with old training/validation mates. A separately prespecified hash-unexposed sensitivity subset addresses only observed prepared-group overlap, changes sample composition, and does not prove patient independence or absence of other related old images.

Bootstrap intervals condition on the observed sample and fixed fitted checkpoints. They omit training randomness and dataset/source uncertainty; boundary or identical predictions can yield degenerate intervals that do not prove certainty or equivalence.
Unadjusted exploratory intervals across multiple candidates, endpoints and readers must not be treated as confirmatory significance or used to select a model on the test set.
Reader labels concern these fixed images, not prospective clinical diagnosis; a fixed reader panel is not a random sample of neuroradiologists.
Clinical AD/CN is a separate endpoint from the four legacy stages. MCI remains prediction-only and is excluded from binary accuracy denominators.

Clinical exact binomial intervals assume independent, representative source subjects. Tiny, selected cohorts, source confounding and preprocessing inspection limit interpretation; one external AD subject cannot establish stable sensitivity.
